title: Practice Test 20
description: A full-length adaptive digital SAT practice test: 98 questions, two modules per section, with an explanation for every question.

questions.passage:
The following text is from Lilliam Rivera's 2020 novel *Never Look Back*. The text describes the narrator arriving at his father's apartment.
"Pops, I'm here!" I drop my bag and set my guitar case against a wall. I place my keys on the bowl right next to the ceramic elephant Pops got me on one of his trips to Santo Domingo when I was a little kid.
questions.prompt: As used in the text, what does the word "drop" most nearly mean?
questions.explanation: The narrator sets down his bag on arriving, so *drop* means "put down." Nothing is unbolted, forgotten, or erased.

questions.passage:
The following text is from Rudolfo Anaya's 1972 novel *Bless Me, Ultima*. The young narrator and his friend Cico are staring into the water of a stream in rural New Mexico.
The golden fish swam by gracefully, cautiously, as if testing the water after a long sleep in his subterranean waters. His powerful tail moved in slow strokes as he slid through the water towards us.
questions.prompt: As used in the text, what does the word "testing" most nearly mean?
questions.explanation: The fish moves "cautiously," as if checking the water after a long sleep, so it is *trying out* the water.

questions.passage: *Life Among the Paiutes* is an 1882 autobiographical narrative by Sarah Winnemucca Hopkins, a Northern Paiute author, educator, and activist. In the work, Winnemucca directly addresses the reader to explain certain customs, writing ______
questions.prompt: Which quotation from *Life Among the Paiutes* most effectively illustrates the claim?
choices: "But how can I describe the scene that followed? Some of you, dear readers, can imagine."
"Now, my dear reader, there is no word so endearing as the word father, and that is why [my people] call all good people father or mother."
"During the time my grandfather was away in California, where he [stayed] till after the Mexican war, there was a girl-baby born in our family."
"We would all go in company to see if the flowers we were looking for had bloomed."
questions.explanation: The claim has two parts: Winnemucca speaks directly to the reader ("my dear reader") and explains a custom. Only B does both: it addresses the reader and explains why her people "call all good people father or mother." A addresses readers but explains no custom; C and D explain no custom to the reader.

questions.passage: In her book *Limitarianism*, researcher Ingrid Robeyns criticizes economic policies that allow businesses to profit from their successes while displacing the burden of failure onto taxpayers. As an example she cites the US financial crisis of 2008 in which dozens of institutions including JPMorgan Chase and SunTrust received a collective \$700 billion of government support. Had the US government previously exercised stricter regulation of risky financial instruments, Robeyns argues, this enormous expenditure of taxpayer dollars would not have been necessary.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main topic of the text?
choices: Consequences of the 2008 financial crisis for JPMorgan Chase and SunTrust
How the US government used money received from taxation to help institutions recover from a period of financial instability
Techniques of assessing the risks of particular methods of financial investment
Why a scholar believes it would be beneficial for certain governmental economic practices to be reconsidered
questions.explanation: Robeyns criticizes policies that shift the cost of failure to taxpayers and argues that stricter regulation would have made the 2008 bailout unnecessary. The text is about why she thinks these government practices should be reconsidered. A and B focus on details of the example; C is never discussed.

questions.passage: The 1978 recording "Two Doors Down" established Dolly Parton as a key figure in pop music. But before she dabbled in pop, her singing and songwriting had been ______ the traditional folk music of the Appalachian Mountains. For example, "Little Bird," one of her best early songs, is clearly influenced by the phrasing and subject matter of Appalachian ballads.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: "Little Bird" is "clearly influenced by" Appalachian ballads, so her early music was *rooted in* that folk tradition.

questions.passage: While no one doubts that politicians are influenced by a variety of incentives, it is generally agreed that they seek to support policies their constituents favor—after all, they risk losing office if they do not. Direct contact with constituents via such means as public events and emails from voters is a major source of politicians' beliefs about their constituents' views, but it is susceptible to a selection effect. There is little reason to presume that individuals with the time, resources, and strength of feeling to directly engage with their representatives are themselves broadly representative.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: People who are likely to contact their elected representatives do not tend to be representative of politicians' constituents generally.
Direct contact with constituents shapes politicians' beliefs about policies their constituents favor, and they try to act in accordance with those beliefs.
Politicians aim to advocate for their constituents' policy preferences, but politicians' understanding of those preferences may be skewed.
Although politicians have an incentive to act in accordance with their constituents' views, that is not the only incentive that influences their policy decisions.
questions.explanation: Politicians try to support what constituents favor, but their sense of those views comes partly from direct contact, which is subject to a "selection effect": the people who make contact are not representative. So their understanding may be skewed. A is only a supporting detail; D repeats the opening concession.

questions.passage: In the seventeenth century, market-savvy British greenhouses scrambled to cultivate ______ the small group of wealthy consumers who could afford to import them from the Caribbean, the fruits had become a status symbol.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "British greenhouses scrambled to cultivate pineapples" is a complete sentence, and "For the small group ... the fruits had become a status symbol" is another. A period separates them. B and C run the two sentences together, and D creates a fragment.

questions.passage: Many ranching terms come from Spanish. For example, the word "rodeo" (a roundup) ______ from the Spanish word *rodear*, and "cinch" (a belt) derives from *cincho*. This is because the first Anglo, African, and Native American cattle ranchers in the southwestern US learned the trade from Spanish-speaking Mexican *vaqueros*, or cowboys.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular "the word 'rodeo'," and the parallel clause uses the present tense ("derives"). So the verb is the singular present *derives*.

questions.passage: An intern at a publishing house who is writing a report is asked to determine which of several genres of books published in 2019 had paperbacks with the lowest average price. Consulting the table, she determines that, on average, the least expensive paperbacks in that year belonged to the genre of ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the assertion?
questions.explanation: In the 2019 column, body, mind, and spirit paperbacks averaged \$18.92, far below the other genres (\$41.93, \$42.85, and \$49.61).

questions.passage: Jose Guerrero, an American abstract painter whose works are distinctive for their energetic brushstrokes, ______ frequently included in the mid-twentieth-century art movement the New York School, whose members were known for capturing the energy and chaos of modern living in paint.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The subject is "Jose Guerrero," which is singular (the phrase between the commas describes him). The verb must be singular: *is*. A, B, and C are plural forms.

questions.passage: Alternative-history fiction is a subgenre of science fiction in which plots center on "what if?" questions. __What if India had started the Industrial Revolution? What if Soviet cosmonauts had been first to land on the moon?__ Speculative counterfactuals like these can be great fodder for stories, but they're also commonly deployed by academic historians to better understand factors influencing historical events. Well-realized and coherent alternative-history stories can thus complement historians' speculations about the past.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?
choices: It provides examples of the types of scenarios addressed in alternative-history fiction.
It illustrates how academic historians have influenced writers of alternative-history fiction.
It indicates specific ideas that were first raised by writers of alternative-history fiction and that subsequently inspired scholarship by academic historians.
It acknowledges counterfactual questions that academic historians have largely overlooked.
questions.explanation: The underlined questions ("What if India had started the Industrial Revolution?") are examples of the "what if?" scenarios that alternative-history fiction centers on.

questions.passage: The Egyptian calendar ______ three seasons: Akhet (the inundation season), Peret (the growing season), and Shemu (the harvest season).
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Had" is the verb, and "three seasons" is its object. No punctuation should come between a verb and its object. The colon after "seasons" then introduces the list.

questions.passage: Some farms are expanding their mix of crop species in an effort to reduce nonagricultural biodiversity loss caused by increasing agricultural specialization, in which farmers focus on a limited range of crops or livestock species to improve yields and, thus, their revenues. To study the joint environmental and economic effects of diversification practices (which can encompass improved soil and water management as well as increased variety in crops and livestock), Laura Vang Rasmussen and team analyzed data from 2,655 farms in eleven countries. They found that using multiple diversification practices concurrently had greater potential for improving both nonagricultural biodiversity and yields than using a single strategy did. Their finding suggests that
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: farmers who focus primarily on increasing crop variety without engaging in other diversification practices will likely help reverse nonagricultural biodiversity loss, but their farms will produce smaller yields than if they had continued to focus on developing a single crop.

it is more expensive to increase crop variety while simultaneously implementing other diversification practices than it is to increase crop variety and then subsequently implement other diversification practices.

farmers who are reluctant to switch from specializing in a single crop to cultivating a variety of crops incorrectly assume that any improvements in yields will be insufficient to offset the costs associated with making that transition.

agricultural diversification doesn't inherently involve a trade-off between environmental and economic considerations, but farmers' chances of avoiding that outcome may be diminished if they focus on crop variety to the exclusion of other diversification practices.
questions.explanation: Using several practices together helped both biodiversity *and* yields more than a single strategy. So diversification need not trade environmental gains for economic ones, but focusing only on crop variety (a single strategy) may reduce that benefit. A claims smaller yields; B and C bring in costs and assumptions the text never discusses.

questions.passage: Though they are in different countries, the towns of Jamame, Somalia, and Nyahururu, Kenya, ______ They are among the rare places that sit almost directly on the equator.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: do they have something in common.
do they have something in common?
questions.explanation: The sentence is a statement, not a question, so it ends with a period, and normal word order is "they do have." The subject "the towns" already comes before the blank, so D completes it: "the towns ... do have something in common."

questions.passage: In World War II, US cryptanalyst Ann Caracristi ______ a code revealing the locations of enemy supply ships.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The sentence needs a main verb for the subject "Ann Caracristi." Only the past-tense *cracked* works; the other choices are not finite verbs.

questions.passage: The fifteenth-century English Heege Manuscript is unusual among collections of its kind and time given its focus on scary stories over more acclaimed works by celebrated medieval authors like Hoccleve. But according to professor James Wade, even more unusually, the three texts in the manuscript's first booklet were likely copied by Richard Heege from a traveling minstrel's repertoire book. The evidence includes performative elements such as the narrator directly appealing to the audience, joking about peasants and royalty, and making jokes that could be modified to refer to the town of Holbrooke when in nearby Radford to avoid giving offense.
questions.prompt: As presented in the text, Wade would most likely agree with which statement about the first booklet of the Heege Manuscript?
choices: The texts it includes were based on stories about the area around Holbrooke and Radford, but these names were later removed.
It was copied from a text that originated from a traveling minstrel who worked in the area around Holbrooke and Radford
It was likely a copy Heege intended to give to a traveling minstrel working in the area around Holbrooke and Radford.
It was written down by Heege from memory based on a performance by a traveling minstrel who worked in the area around Radford and Brackonwet.
questions.explanation: Wade thinks the texts were copied "from a traveling minstrel's repertoire book," and the jokes could be adjusted for Holbrooke or Radford, so the minstrel worked in that area. The names were not removed (A), Heege did not give the copy to a minstrel (C), and nothing suggests writing from memory or mentions Brackonwet (D).

questions.passage: Water is constantly moving and changing forms on Earth and in the atmosphere. This process is called the water cycle, and it is typically thought to consist of evaporation, condensation, and precipitation. However, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration seeks ______ understanding of the water cycle to include transpiration, sublimation, and other types of water movement.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Seeks" must be followed by an infinitive: "seeks *to expand* understanding."

questions.passage: The moon Dia orbits Jupiter in the same direction that the planet rotates. ______ Dia's orbit is described as prograde. Helike, another of Jupiter's moons, orbits in the opposite direction, so its orbit is described with the opposite term: retrograde.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Dia orbits in the same direction the planet rotates; *therefore* its orbit is called prograde. "Thus" signals this result.

questions.passage: To determine the approximate age of ocher artifacts excavated from an archaeological site in China, archaeologist Fa-Gang Wang and colleagues collected samples of sediments surrounding the ocher artifacts; these samples were then analyzed using a method known as optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) dating. ______ OSL dating indicated that the ocher artifacts were between 39,000 and 41,000 years old.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The text describes a sequence: collect samples, analyze them with OSL dating, and finally get the age. "Ultimately" introduces the final result.

questions.passage: William Bowditch's home in Massachusetts was one of dozens of stops on the underground railroad (the network of people and places that some enslaved people used to escape to freedom). The word "underground" may lead one to assume that Bowditch kept his antislavery views a secret. ______ his views were quite well known.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The text raises an assumption (that Bowditch kept his views secret) and then corrects it: his views were well known. "On the contrary" introduces this contradiction.

questions.passage: *The Wonderful Wizard of Oz* is a 1900 novel by L. Frank Baum. In the novel, Dorothy travels to meet the Wizard of Oz, an important figure in a place called the Emerald City. The text presents a contrast between the Wizard of Oz's self-presentation and reality: ______
questions.prompt: Which quotation from *The Wonderful Wizard of Oz* most effectively illustrates the claim?
choices: "[The hot air balloon] came down gradually, and I was not hurt a bit. But I found myself in the midst of a strange people, who, seeing me come from the clouds, thought I was a great Wizard."
"When I grew up I became a ventriloquist, and at that I was very well trained by a great master."
"Then Oz got into the basket and said to all the people in a loud voice: 'I am now going away to make a visit.'"
"'I am Oz, the Great and Terrible,' said the little man, in a trembling voice."
questions.explanation: The contrast is between how Oz presents himself and what he is. In D he announces himself as "the Great and Terrible," but he is "the little man" speaking "in a trembling voice."

questions.passage: The interiors of many temples in the ancient Middle East needed to satisfy a precise set of acoustic demands: the sounds of chants and hymns should travel with clarity, while profound silences should be fully felt and appreciated. In a research paper, a student claims that the users of one such temple were aware of how the materials that were used within the structure could affect sound quality and that they deliberately applied this knowledge to influence how sound was experienced in the space.
questions.prompt: Which quotation from a work by a historian would most directly support the student's claim?
choices: "The acoustic environment of the temple was best suited for music that eschewed ornamentation in favor of simple melodies, harmonies, and rhythms."
"Many researchers believe that the central chamber of the temple had a high ceiling, a feature that has since become essential to the acoustic design of modern concert halls."
"During special occasions, curtains were placed inside the temple to minimize reverberation and confine the sound to designated locations."
"The innermost room of the temple was likely among the quietest spaces in the interior of the temple."
questions.explanation: The claim is that the temple users knew materials affect sound and *deliberately* used that knowledge. Placing curtains to reduce reverberation is a deliberate use of a material to shape sound. A, B, and D describe acoustic features but show no deliberate use of materials.

questions.passage: Tardigrades, tiny animals often called water bears, are remarkably ______: they can survive being dried out for years, frozen to near absolute zero, and even exposed to the vacuum of space.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Surviving drying, freezing, and space shows the animals are tough, or *hardy*. *Fragile* means the opposite.

questions.passage: Before the printing press, books in Europe were copied by hand, a slow process that made them expensive. Johannes Gutenberg's press, developed around 1450, made it possible to ______ books far more quickly, and prices soon fell.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: The press made it faster to make books, which lowered prices. *Produce* means "make."

questions.passage: Octavia E. Butler's 1979 novel *Kindred* sends its narrator, a Black woman living in 1970s California, back in time to a plantation in early-nineteenth-century Maryland. Rather than treating time travel as an adventure, Butler uses it to ______ the brutal realities of slavery, forcing both the narrator and the reader to confront them directly.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Butler makes the narrator and reader "confront" slavery's realities, so she uses time travel to *expose* them. *Conceal* is the opposite.

questions.passage: Although the Atacama Desert in Chile is one of the driest places on Earth, it is not ______ of life: microbes survive inside salt rocks, drawing water from the humid air that the salt absorbs.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: "Not devoid of life" means not completely empty of life, which fits the microbes that survive there.

questions.passage: Honeybees that find a good source of food return to the hive and perform a "waggle dance." The angle of the dance shows other bees the direction of the food relative to the Sun, and the length of the waggling shows how far away it is. Zoologist Karl von Frisch, who decoded the dance, received a Nobel Prize in 1973 for this and related work.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
choices: To explain how honeybees use a dance to share information about food
To argue that honeybees are more intelligent than other insects
To describe how von Frisch became interested in studying bees
To compare the diets of honeybees and other pollinators
questions.explanation: The text explains what the dance communicates (direction and distance of food). B, C, and D are not discussed.

questions.passage: Many people picture deserts as lifeless sand dunes. Yet only about 20 percent of the world's deserts are covered by sand. Most are made up of rocky plains, gravel, and mountains, and many support plants and animals specially adapted to dry conditions.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It describes a type of landscape and then explains how it formed.
It compares two deserts and then explains why one is larger.
It presents a common view of deserts and then corrects it with facts.
It lists several animals and then describes where each one lives.
questions.explanation: The text opens with a common picture (deserts as sand dunes) and then shows it is mostly wrong (only about 20 percent is sand).

questions.passage:
**Text 1**
For decades, many scientists assumed that birds could not be very intelligent because their brains are small. A bird's brain lacks the layered structure found in the cortex of mammals, which was thought to be necessary for complex thought.
**Text 2**
Crows and parrots can solve multistep puzzles, use tools, and remember where they hid food months earlier. Researchers have found that bird brains pack their neurons much more densely than mammal brains do, so a small bird brain can hold as many neurons as a much larger primate brain.
questions.prompt: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the assumption described in Text 1?
choices: By agreeing that a layered cortex is required for complex thought
By suggesting that scientists have not yet tested whether birds can use tools
By claiming that crows and parrots have larger brains than most primates
By arguing that brain size alone is a poor guide to intelligence, since bird brains are densely packed with neurons
questions.explanation: Text 1 says small brains were thought to mean low intelligence. Text 2 shows birds solving complex problems and explains that their small brains are packed with neurons, so size alone is misleading.

questions.passage: The Great Wall of China is not a single wall. It is a series of walls and fortifications built and rebuilt by different dynasties over roughly two thousand years. Many sections were made of packed earth, while the famous stone and brick sections near Beijing were mostly built during the Ming dynasty (1368–1644).
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: The Great Wall was built entirely of stone and brick.
The Great Wall is a collection of structures built over many centuries.
The Ming dynasty began building the Great Wall in 1368.
The Great Wall's earth sections were stronger than its stone sections.
questions.explanation: The text says the wall is "a series of walls" built by different dynasties over about two thousand years. A and C contradict it; D is never stated.

questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from Willa Cather's 1913 novel *O Pioneers!* Alexandra Bergson has just taken over her family's farm on the Nebraska prairie.
For the first time, perhaps, since that land emerged from the waters of geologic ages, a human face was set toward it with love and yearning. It seemed beautiful to her, rich and strong and glorious. Her eyes drank in the breadth of it, until her tears blinded her.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Alexandra feels a deep love for the prairie land.
Alexandra is worried that the land will be difficult to farm.
Alexandra is overwhelmed by sadness about leaving the land.
Alexandra is curious about how the land was formed.

questions.passage: The name "Silk Road" suggests a single highway, but a student claims that it was really a network of many routes linking China with Central Asia, the Middle East, and the Mediterranean.
questions.prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the student's claim?

Goods from the same period have been found along several separate paths, some crossing mountains and others following coastlines.
Most traders traveled only part of the distance between China and the Mediterranean.
The term "Silk Road" was first used by a geographer in the nineteenth century.
questions.explanation: The claim is that there were many routes. Finding trade goods along several separate paths shows exactly that. A, C, and D do not address how many routes there were.

questions.passage: A student claims that people often remember an unfinished task better than a finished one, an idea known as the Zeigarnik effect.
questions.prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the student's claim?
choices: Participants who finished all their assigned puzzles reported feeling more satisfied than those who did not.
Participants who were interrupted before finishing some puzzles later recalled more of the interrupted puzzles than of the completed ones.
Participants recalled puzzles they found easy more often than puzzles they found difficult.
Participants who were given more time completed a greater number of puzzles.
questions.explanation: The claim compares memory for unfinished and finished tasks. B shows interrupted (unfinished) puzzles were remembered better than completed ones.

questions.passage: A student is comparing the heights of four famous waterfalls. Looking at the table, the student notes that the tallest of the four is ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
questions.explanation: Angel Falls is listed at 979 meters, the greatest height in the table.

questions.passage: A city surveyed residents about how they usually get to work. The student who analyzed the survey claims that in both years shown, more residents drove alone than used all other methods combined.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the student's claim?
choices: In 2010, 30% of residents used public transit, and in 2020, 22% did.
In 2010, 58% of residents drove alone, and in 2020, 54% did.
In 2020, the share of residents who walked or biked was greater than in 2010.
In 2010 and 2020, fewer than 15% of residents walked or biked.

questions.passage: Sea otters eat large numbers of sea urchins, and sea urchins eat kelp. In areas along the Pacific coast where sea otters were hunted almost to extinction, urchin populations grew rapidly and kelp forests largely disappeared. This suggests that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: sea urchins prefer to eat other foods when kelp is scarce.
kelp forests grow fastest in areas without sea urchins or sea otters.
the presence of sea otters helps protect kelp forests.
sea otters depend on kelp as their main source of food.
questions.explanation: When otters disappeared, urchins increased and kelp vanished. So otters, by eating urchins, help kelp survive.

questions.passage: In the 1950s, many scientists thought the continents had always been in fixed positions. When Marie Tharp mapped the floor of the Atlantic Ocean, she found a deep valley running down the center of a long underwater mountain ridge. Because such a valley could form where Earth's crust is being pulled apart, Tharp's map ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: proved that the Atlantic Ocean is shrinking over time.
showed that underwater mountains are older than mountains on land.
provided evidence that the continents on either side of the Atlantic may be moving apart.
suggested that the Atlantic floor is flat in most places.
questions.explanation: A valley where the crust is pulled apart down the middle of the Atlantic suggests the two sides are separating, supporting moving continents. A says the opposite; B and D are not supported.

questions.passage: The Andes, which stretch about 7,000 kilometers along the western edge of South America, ______ the longest continental mountain range in the world.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
